lesson.title: A digit and its place value
lesson.subtitle: Distinguish a digit from its value
lesson.story: Each column groups blocks by value. A hundreds block represents 100, a tens rod represents 10 and a ones counter represents 1. An empty column represents zero in that place.
lesson.objective: Read base-ten models and reason about the tens place.

steps.title: Find the place
hints: Each block in the tens column represents 10.

steps.title: Find the place value
steps.prompt: What is the value of the digit in the tens place?
hints: Count the blocks in the tens column.
The tens place uses groups of 10.
There are 6 blocks in the tens column; each represents 10.
The digit in the tens place has value 6 × 10 = 60.

steps.title: Explain the place
steps.prompt: Why does a digit need a named place?

choices.label: Zero means the other columns must also be empty.
Every digit stands for single ones, wherever it sits.
The place tells us how much each digit represents.

hints: Look at the different column units.
A hundreds block and a ones counter have different values.
The place tells us whether to count hundreds, tens or ones.
Choose: The place tells us how much each digit represents.
